{"content":"# Helper for checking classes gets wrong answers and confusing errors

## What happens now

When I ask the helper whether something has attributes, it gives wrong answers and the wrong kind of errors. Handing it an instance of a class is accepted and silently turned into its class. Asking about an ordinary class such as the built-in integer class raises an error about a type instead of simply saying no. The dictionary helper has the same loose handling of instances. The description of one attribute has no written explanation, it is not reachable by name from the package, and the documentation page has no help section at all.

## What should happen

I want to hand a class to the helper and get a plain yes or no, and to hand it something that is not a class at all and get a clear message saying exactly that. A class with no attributes should be reported as a wrong value rather than a wrong type. The dictionary helper should look at each value's class the same way. I also want one description of an attribute available under the package name and written down in the documentation page, together with a help section that shows examples for the three helpers.

## About this project

attrs is a small Python library that lets you write classes with less repetition by listing their attributes in a short, readable block instead of writing out an initializer, a comparison, and a text form by hand. It also offers a few helper functions for inspecting such classes and turning them into plain dictionaries.

## Problem this solves

I keep code that accepts anything and has to check it before using it, so I need a trustworthy yes or no answer about whether a class was written with attrs. Today the check swallows the wrong kind of error and cannot tell me that I passed something that is not a class, so my guard clauses either pass bad input through or crash with a message that does not match what I did.

## What changed

The check helper now only accepts classes, says no for a normal class that has no attributes, and raises a clear type error for anything that is not a class. The list helper behaves the same way and reports a class without attributes as a wrong value instead of a wrong type. Instances are no longer accepted by the list helper. The dictionary helper looks at the class of each value when deciding to go deeper. The attribute description is now listed among the names the package exports, it carries a written explanation of the name, the default value, and the default maker, and the documentation page gained a help section with worked examples.

Ease of use and correctness of the checking helpers, plus better documentation.

After: asking about the built-in integer class simply returns no, and passing an instance gives me a message telling me a class is what is wanted, so I know exactly which mistake I made.

## What should happen

Asking for the attributes of a class gives a clear error if I pass an object instead of a class, and gives a separate, clear error if the class has no fields. The attribute listing can be turned into a plain dictionary, including nested dictionaries when the fields point at other attrs classes. ## About this project

This is a small library for describing classes with less repetition. You list the fields of a class once and the library builds the class for you, including its text form, its equality, its hash, and the way new objects are created, with switches to turn each of those off.

## Problem this solves

Because the tool accepts an object where a class was meant, a mistake in my own code passes silently and I get results about something other than what I asked for. And since nothing is written down, I cannot tell which of my classes are attrs classes without running them and reading the source.

## What changed

Listing attributes now refuses objects and points at the class instead, and reports a missing-fields problem with its own error rather than the type error. The attribute information object is now available from the main package entry point next to the other helpers, so I can get at it without reaching into a private module. Every helper, argument, switch, and returned field is described in writing, and the documentation page now has a full reference with runnable examples.

## Impact

Correctness of errors, ease of use, and documentation.

## User experience

Before: I pass an object where I meant a class, and the listing quietly answers for the object's class, so I never find out I made a mistake. And the documentation page is empty, so I cannot learn the rules from reading.

After: I pass an object where I meant a class and I get told straight away that a class is needed. I pass a plain class with no fields and I get told the class has no fields. The documentation page now shows every helper with its arguments and runnable examples.
